title: Reference frames and relative motion; Projectile motion; Systems and center of mass
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: K05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; K05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D07-1#N.2, K05-1#N.3, D07-1#N.7, K05-1#N.16a, D07-1#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Reference frame
items.clue: An observer with a ruler and a clock.

items.label: Range
items.clue: Horizontal distance a projectile covers between launch and landing.

items.label: Horizontal component
items.clue: Part of the launch velocity that never changes, as no force acts that way.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: Quantity that comes out the same for two observers in steady relative motion.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rod is made of a 0.50 m aluminium section joined end to end to a 0.50 m steel section of the same diameter. Each section is uniform, and the steel section has the greater mass. How does the location of the rod's centre of mass compare with the rod's midpoint?

options.text: It is at the midpoint, since the rod's shape is symmetric about that point.
It is on the aluminium side of the midpoint, nearer the lighter section.
It is at the centre of the steel section, the more massive part.
It lies between the midpoint and the centre of the steel section.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides east at 6 m s⁻¹ relative to the road. Observer X stands beside the road. Observer Y is in a car that moves east along the same road at a constant 10 m s⁻¹. Which statement correctly compares the cyclist's velocity as measured by Y with the velocity measured by X?

options.text: Y measures the same velocity as X does, 6 m s⁻¹ east along the road.
Y measures a smaller speed than X does, and in the opposite direction.
Y measures a larger speed than X does, and in the same direction.
Y measures a smaller speed than X does, in the same direction.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of mass 2m and length L has a small ball of mass m fixed to one end. How far from the other end of the rod is the centre of mass of the rod–ball system?

A moving walkway in an airport moves at constant velocity v_W relative to the floor. A passenger walks on the walkway with velocity v_P relative to the walkway. A worker walks on the floor beside the walkway at constant velocity v_F relative to the floor. All three velocities are components along the same straight line. Which expression gives the passenger's velocity as measured by the worker?

options.text: v_P − v_W − v_F
v_P + v_W + v_F
v_F − v_P − v_W
v_P + v_W − v_F

questions.stem: A diver makes two dives from the same springboard. In each dive, her center of mass leaves the board from the same height with the same velocity. In dive 1 she keeps her body straight; in dive 2 she pulls into a tight tuck soon after leaving the board. Air resistance is negligible. How do the maximum heights reached by her center of mass in the two dives compare?

options.text: Dive 2's is greater, since pulling into a tuck lifts her body higher.
They cannot be compared, since a rotating object is not a projectile.
They are equal, since her center of mass moves as a projectile in both dives.
Dive 1's is greater, since her outstretched body reaches higher.
